<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["chest pressure or pain", "pain spreading to arm or jaw", "sweating or shortness of breath"], "concern": "possible heart attack"}</triage>
What you're describing - chest pressure spreading to your arm or jaw, with sweating or shortness of breath - can be a heart attack. This can't wait. Call 911 right now, and don't drive yourself to the hospital.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["face drooping", "arm or leg weakness on one side", "slurred speech"], "concern": "possible stroke"}</triage>
Sudden face drooping, weakness on one side, or slurred speech can be a sign of a stroke. Minutes matter - treatment is most effective when it starts right away. Call 911 now and note when the symptoms began.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["face drooping", "face pain or numbness", "arm or leg weakness on one side"], "concern": "possible stroke or TIA"}</triage>
Sudden face drooping, weakness on one side, or slurred speech can be a sign of a stroke, even if it has already gone away. Minutes matter. Call 911 right away and note when the symptoms began.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["vomiting blood", "black tarry stools"], "concern": "possible bleeding in the stomach or intestines"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. Vomiting blood or black tarry stools can be a sign of bleeding in the digestive tract, which can become serious quickly. Please go to the emergency department now, or call 911 if you feel faint.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["shortness of breath", "sharp chest pain", "recent surgery or long travel"], "concern": "possible blood clot in the lung"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. Shortness of breath with sharp chest pain, especially after surgery or a long trip, can be a sign of a blood clot in the lung. Please call 911 or go to the emergency department now.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["swelling of lips", "tongue or throat", "trouble breathing", "hives after exposure"], "concern": "possible severe allergic reaction"}</triage>
Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat with trouble breathing can be a severe allergic reaction. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it now, and call 911.

<triage>{"level": "URGENT", "red_flags": ["new flashes of light", "sudden increase in floaters"], "concern": "possible retinal tear or early retinal detachment"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. New flashes of light or a sudden shower of floaters can be a sign of a retinal tear, which can lead to detachment and permanent vision loss. You should have a dilated eye exam today. If a curtain or shadow appears or you lose vision, go to the emergency department right away.

<triage>{"level": "URGENT", "red_flags": ["one-sided leg swelling", "calf pain and warmth"], "concern": "possible blood clot in the leg"}</triage>
Swelling, pain, and warmth in one calf can be a sign of a blood clot in the leg, which can travel to the lungs. This should be checked today. Call 911 if you develop chest pain or trouble breathing.

<triage>{"level": "URGENT", "red_flags": ["fever with flank or back pain", "burning with urination"], "concern": "possible kidney infection"}</triage>
Thank you for sharing that. Burning when you urinate plus fever and pain in your side or back can mean the infection has spread up to the kidney. This needs treatment today. If you can't keep fluids down, or you feel confused or faint, go to the emergency department.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["chest pressure or pain", "pain spreading to arm or jaw", "sweating or shortness of breath"], "concern": "possible heart attack"}</triage>
What you're describing - chest pressure spreading to your arm or jaw, with sweating or shortness of breath - can be a sign of a heart attack. Minutes matter here. Call 911 right now and do not drive yourself to the hospital.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["face drooping", "face numbness", "arm or leg weakness on one side"], "concern": "possible stroke or TIA"}</triage>
Sudden face drooping, numbness on one side, or weakness in an arm or leg can be a sign of a stroke, even if it has already gone away. Minutes matter. Call 911 right away and note when the symptoms began.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["vomiting blood", "black tarry stools"], "concern": "possible bleeding in the stomach or intestines"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. Vomiting blood or black tarry stools can be a sign of bleeding in the digestive tract, which can become serious quickly. Please go to the emergency department now, or call 911 if you feel faint.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["sudden severe headache", "worst headache of life"], "concern": "possible bleeding in the brain"}</triage>
A headache that hits suddenly and is the worst of your life can be a sign of bleeding in the brain. This needs emergency evaluation right away. Please call 911 now rather than driving yourself.

<triage>{"level": "SOON", "red_flags": ["new breast lump"], "concern": "breast change that needs evaluation"}</triage>
A new breast lump is the most common reason for a breast exam, and most lumps are not cancer. But any new lump should be checked by a clinician, and sometimes needs imaging. Please book a visit in the next few days.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "likely common cold"}</triage>
A couple of days of runny nose, sore throat, and mild cough with no high fever usually means a common cold. Rest, fluids, and over-the-counter remedies can help. If it goes on for more than 10 days, or if you have a high fever, get seen.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "likely muscle strain"}</triage>
Stiffness in the lower back after activity, without numbness, leg weakness, or bladder or bowel changes, is usually a muscle strain. Rest, gentle movement, heat, and over-the-counter pain relief help most people. Book a visit if it isn't getting better within a couple of weeks.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "likely mild allergic reaction"}</triage>
An itchy rash that bares no spreading redness, no wheezing, and no hives usually isn't serious. Antihistamines often help. If it spreads, gets hotter, or adds new symptoms, get seen.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["face drooping", "arm or leg weakness on one side", "slurred speech"], "concern": "possible stroke"}</triage>
Sudden face drooping, weakness on one side, or slurred speech can be a sign of a stroke. Minutes matter - treatment is most effective when it starts right away. Call 911 now and note when the symptoms began.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["chest pressure or pain", "pain spreading to arm or jaw", "sweating or shortness of breath"], "concern": "possible heart attack"}</triage>
What you're describing - chest pressure spreading to the arm or jaw, with sweating or shortness of breath - can be a heart attack. This can't wait. Call 911 right now, and don't drive yourself to the hospital.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["fever in a baby under 3 months"], "concern": "possible serious infection in a young infant"}</triage>
A temperature of 100.4 F (38 C) or higher in a baby younger than 3 months can be a sign of a serious infection, even if the baby looks okay. Please take your baby to the emergency department now.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["swelling of lips", "tongue or throat", "trouble breathing", "hives after exposure"], "concern": "possible severe allergic reaction"}</triage>
Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat along with trouble breathing can be a severe allergic reaction. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it now, and call 911.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["sudden vision loss", "curtain or shadow over vision"], "concern": "possible retinal detachment or blocked blood vessel in the eye"}</triage>
A curtain, shadow, or sudden loss of vision in one eye is an eye emergency - it can mean the retina is detaching or a blood vessel is blocked. Please go to the emergency department now, or call 911 if you can't focus on anything else.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["thoughts of suicide or self-harm"], "concern": "risk of self-harm"}</triage>
I'm so sorry you're feeling this way, and I'm glad you told me. Right now, please call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) - they are there to listen at any hour. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

<triage>{"level": "URGENT", "red_flags": ["spreading redness and warmth", "red streaks", "fever with a skin wound"], "concern": "possible spreading skin infection"}</triage>
I'm glad you mentioned this. Redness that is spreading, feels hot, or has red streaks - especially with fever - can be a skin infection moving deeper into tissue. It should be looked at today. If it spreads quickly, call 911.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["chest pressure or pain", "pain spreading to arm or jaw", "sweating or shortness of breath", "recent surgery or long travel"], "concern": "possible heart attack"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. What you're describing - chest pressure spreading to your arm or jaw, with sweating or shortness of breath - can be a sign of a heart attack. Minutes matter here. Call 911 right away and do not drive yourself to the hospital.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["trembling", "sweating", "fast heartbeat", "chest pressure or pain"], "concern": "possible severe allergic reaction or heart issue"}</triage>
Trembling, sweating, a fast heartbeat, and chest pressure can be a severe allergic reaction or a sign of a heart problem. These symptoms can get worse quickly. Please call 911 now, or drive to the emergency department if you are too unwell to drive.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["sudden vision loss", "curtain or shadow over vision"], "concern": "possible retinal detachment or blocked blood vessel in the eye"}</triage>
A curtain, shadow, or sudden loss of vision in one eye is an eye emergency - it can mean the retina is detaching or a blood vessel is blocked. Waiting can cause permanent vision loss. Please go to the emergency department right away.

What symptoms are you noticing, how long has this been going on, and is anything getting worse?

<triage>{"level": "NEEDS_INFO", "red_flags": [], "concern": ""}</triage>

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "general health question"}</triage>
Most headaches are not serious, but some are not. A headache that is sudden and severe, like the worst of your life, can be a bleeding in the brain. A headache that gets worse with bending or coughing, or that comes with fever and a stiff neck, should be checked. A headache that is constant and a new way of seeing, like flashing lights, should be seen today.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "general health question"}</triage>
A TIA, or transient ischemic attack, is a temporary blockage of blood flow to the brain that causes stroke-like symptoms that go away within hours. A stroke is a permanent blockage or bleeding in the brain. TIAs are considered warning signs and should be checked right away, even though they don't cause permanent damage. If you or someone with you has face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking, call 911 even if it has already gone away.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "general health question"}</triage>
Yes, anxiety can cause chest pressure or pain, often with sweating, a fast heartbeat, or shortness of breath. It usually goes away when you calm down. If someone has chest pressure along with jaw or arm pain, or pain that spreads, call 911.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "general health question"}</triage>
A blood clot in the leg usually causes swelling, pain, and warmth in one leg, often starting in the calf. It can be hard to tell from a regular muscle strain, but it shouldn't improve with rest. If you have these symptoms right now, get care today.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "general health question"}</triage>
Floaters that have looked the same for years, or that come with no flashes of light, are usually harmless. A sudden increase, a sudden shower of flashes, or a curtain or shadow over your vision should be checked today.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "general health question"}</triage>
A mole that changes in size, shape, color, or that starts to itch, bleed, or hurt is worth having checked, since those can be early signs of skin cancer. Most moles are not cancerous, and a visit with a dermatologist is usually the way to find out.

<triage>{"level": "NEEDS_INFO", "red_flags": [], "concern": ""}</triage>
What symptoms are you noticing, how long has it been going on, and why is this timing important?

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "likely muscle strain"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. Soreness in the chest after exercise, without pain when breathing or sharp chest pressure, is usually a muscle strain. Staying gently active and keeping fluids up helps. If it isn't improving after a week or two, book a visit.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["chest pressure or pain", "pain spreading to arm or jaw", "sweating or shortness of breath"], "concern": "possible heart attack"}</triage>
Thanks for telling me. What you described - chest pressure spreading to your arm or jaw, with sweating or shortness of breath - can be a sign of a heart attack. Minutes matter here. Call 911 right now and do not drive yourself to the hospital.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "administrative request"}</triage>
Sorry to hear that. You can request a new date through the MyChart section of the app, or ask the care team member you spoke to to send the request to the department. If you have a health question right now, you can type it in the chat box.

<triage>{"level": "SOON", "red_flags": ["recent surgery or long travel"], "concern": "possible blood clot"}</triage>
Thank you for sharing that. A long trip or recent surgery raises the risk of a blood clot in the leg, which can travel to the lungs. If you have calf swelling, calf pain, or trouble breathing, get care right away. Otherwise, book a visit in the next few days to be checked.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "administrative request"}</triage>
I'm glad you mentioned this. Your shot is usually bookable in the Health Hub under "Vaccines". If you're unsure, ask the team at the front desk.

<triage>{"level": "ROUTINE", "red_flags": [], "concern": "typical over-the-counter use"}</triage>
I'm glad you mentioned this. Taking two extra-strength Tylenol every 6 hours is generally safe, but if you have liver disease, a history of bleeding, or are on blood thinners, tell the pharmacy. And go to the emergency department if you vomit blood, have black tarry stools, or feel faint.

<triage>{"level": "EMERGENCY", "red_flags": ["loss of consciousness", "seizure", "recent surgery or a long trip"], "concern": "possible bleeding in the brain"}</triage>
A sudden loss of consciousness, especially with bleeding or a severe headache, can be a sign of bleeding in the brain. Please call 911 now rather than driving yourself.

<triage>{"level": "URGENT", "red_flags": ["rash with fever", "rash near the eyes or on the face"], "concern": "possible serious skin infection"}</triage>
A red, warm, swollen area on the skin that is getting bigger, or a red streak going up toward the eye, can be a spreading skin infection. Fever with a skin rash that burns or stings can be an allergic reaction. These should be seen today.

<triage>{"level": "SOON", "red_flags": ["red streaks going up a limb", "red spot with a red streak"], "concern": "possible spreading skin infection"}</triage>
I'm glad you mentioned this. A red spot that is spreading, especially with red streaks or warmth, can be a sign of a skin infection moving into deeper tissue. It should be looked at today. If you develop fever or chills, go to the emergency department.
